title: Fourplex zoning directed; Weber Street tower deferred
subtitle: Park dedication review, fire truck funding, Registry Theatre agreement, heritage designations and long service volunteer awards
overview: Council directed staff to draft a zoning by-law amendment allowing up to four residential units as of right on lots where single, semi-detached or street townhouse homes are already permitted. Staff will report back in the first quarter of 2024. The motion passed on a recorded vote {{vote:m2}}. It builds on the existing three-unit permission and is tied to housing targets and a federal housing funding application.

Council also deferred a decision on a proposed tall tower at 83-87 Weber Street East to a special meeting on October 30, 2023. The applicant submitted revised plans with more height and density just before the meeting, and staff said they had not had time to review them. A provincial deadline for a decision falls on October 30.

Other decisions included a review of the city's park dedication program for trees, benches and similar tributes, with results due in spring 2024. Council pre-approved the purchase of three fire apparatus, authorized an operating agreement for the Registry Theatre, and approved appointments to advisory committees and the Centre in the Square board. Council also began the process to designate three more properties as heritage sites. The Mayor said the city had sent its response to the province on housing task force recommendations, and the meeting opened with long service awards for volunteer groups.

decisions.detail: Staff were directed to propose a zoning by-law amendment permitting up to four residential units on eligible lots and to report back in Q1 2024, with the motion carried {{vote:m2}}.
Council deferred the Official Plan and zoning amendments for the proposed tower to the October 30, 2023 special meeting so staff can review the applicant's late revisions.
Staff will review the process for dedicating trees, benches and other commemorative items in parks and trails, and report with an implementation plan in spring 2024.
Council pre-approved the purchase of three fire apparatus as outlined in report CSD-2023-468.
The Mayor and Clerk were authorized to sign an operating agreement with the theatre's current operators for the community theatre space at 122 Frederick Street.
The General Manager of Development Services was authorized to sign licence extension agreements as set out in report DSD-2023-435.

decisions.item: Lifting of holding provision at 7 Morrison Road
decisions.detail: Council approved removing Holding Provision 42H from 7 Morrison Road for Klondike Homes Ltd.
Council appointed members to the Committee of Adjustment, Heritage Kitchener and the Arts and Culture Advisory Committee, and reappointed two members to the Centre in the Square Board.

debate: On Weber Street East, staff said the revised, taller design was less compliant with the tall building guidelines' tower separation, which could limit development on neighbouring lands. They also said they had not had time to review the late changes. Several councillors said they were uncomfortable planning on the fly.

The applicant's representatives said fast approvals matter during a housing shortage and that a two-week delay holds up rental units. They said the added height was tied to benefits: some units at a 20% discount for 20 years, higher energy efficiency, and accessible units. Councillors asked about three-bedroom units, which the applicant said would be kept, and about protecting the affordable units if the property were sold.

A resident delegate opposed the Weber Street tower, saying high-rise buildings may not stay affordable or energy-efficient over the long term and that affordability should be tied to income rather than market rent.

On four units as of right, a housing advocacy delegate supported the motion and said it should avoid onerous requirements. Councillors raised affordability, short-term rentals, demolition and displacement, parking, lot sizes, and how the change would apply in heritage districts. Staff said the work could be done by Q1 2024, and that the federal housing funding is competitive and not guaranteed.
On park dedications, councillors said the current process is slow and unclear. They said families value commemorative trees and benches, and they supported a clearer process.
